subject.title: fix(oauth): invalidate cache on server URL changes

question: Should upgrading an existing directory-backed OAuth cache with no recorded server URL intentionally purge its credentials on first use, even when the configured URL has not changed?
rationale: Older directory caches cannot prove which URL issued their credentials, so choosing fail-closed invalidation versus a compatibility-preserving migration is a trust-boundary and upgrade-policy decision rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Approve and document one-time reset
options.body: Keep the fail-closed behavior, add an explicit upgrade note and regression coverage proving that pre-marker caches require reauthentication once.

options.title: Design a compatibility migration
options.body: Preserve pre-marker cache state only through a narrowly defined migration that can establish an endpoint binding without reopening cross-server credential reuse.

recommendation.title: Approve and document one-time reset
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed behavior, add an explicit upgrade note and regression coverage proving that pre-marker caches require reauthentication once.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current OAuth trust-boundary implementation and are best placed to clarify the intended upgrade contract.
